draft.title: Melting point and distillation
card: Melting point
A pure solid melts at one sharp temperature, over a range of about 1°C or less. An impure solid melts over a wider range and at a lower temperature than the pure substance.
Simple distillation
The liquid is heated, its vapour is cooled in a condenser, and the liquid that collects is the distillate. It separates a liquid from a solid, or liquids whose boiling points are far apart.
Fractional distillation
A fractionating column is added between the flask and the condenser. Vapour condenses and re-evaporates many times in the column, so liquids with close boiling points can be separated.
In both methods the liquid with the lower boiling point comes off first. Its vapour is richer in that liquid.
draft.remember: A sharp melting point means pure. Distillation separates liquids by boiling point, and a column is needed when the boiling points are close.

a.q: A student measures the melting point of a white solid from a synthesis. It melts from 118°C to 126°C, and the pure compound melts at 130°C. What does this show?
opts: The solid is impure
The solid is pure
The solid is a liquid mixture
The solid has a high boiling point
a.why: A pure solid melts sharply at its known temperature. A wide range that starts below 130°C shows impurities are present. A high melting point alone does not show purity, because the range is what matters.
a.clue: Look at the width of the range and where it sits.

b.q: A mixture of two liquids, with boiling points of 78°C and 82°C, must be separated. Which method is suitable, and why?
opts: Fractional distillation, as the boiling points are close
Simple distillation, as the boiling points are close
Fractional distillation, as the boiling points are far apart
Simple distillation, as both liquids have low boiling points
b.why: Boiling points only 4°C apart need the repeated condensing and evaporating in a fractionating column. Simple distillation works when the boiling points are far apart, so it would give a mixed distillate here.
b.clue: What does the column add that simple distillation lacks?

b.best: Fractional distillation, as the boiling points are close

problems.detail: 'Its vapour is richer in that liquid' is unclear. 'Its' seems to point to the lower-boiling liquid, which makes the sentence circular. It should say the vapour from the mixture is richer in the lower-boiling liquid.

Why (a) rejects 'a high melting point', but the option says 'high boiling point'. It also says 'the range is what matters', while the card says both a wider range and a lower temperature show impurity. The why does not match the option or fully match the card.
